title: Cunliffe's Homeric grammatical appendix (conditional / relative sentence table)
status: reference material - NOT a served text work
not_served_note: This is reference / bonus material, not part of the served running-text corpus. It is a lexicon-grammatical reference table, not a text edition, so it does NOT enter the source-precedence ladder, is NOT assigned a served work-id, and is NOT listed in corpus_editions.json or the work-id registry. It lives under data/reference/, entirely separate from data/corpus/.

provenance.author: Richard John Cunliffe
provenance.work: A Lexicon of the Homeric Dialect
provenance.appendix_title: TABLE of the Uses of εἰ (αἴ), ἤν in Protasis with the accompanying Apodoses and of the corresponding Relative and Conditional Relative Sentences with Future, Subjunctive and Optative.
provenance.note: First known machine-readable copy of the appendix body. Digital editions (Perseus/Scaife, Logeion, ATLAS/exploreHomer, jtauber's cunliffe) reproduce only the pointers into the table, not the table itself; the pre-existing Google OCR of the scan renders the polytonic Greek unusably.

license.derived_dataset: CC BY-SA 4.0 (matching the corpus). The structured/OCR'd dataset is the corpus maintainers' to license; the underlying text is public domain.

code_legend.description: A construction code such as III.B.a.1 decomposes by level.
code_legend.roman_I_II_III: Logical type of the εἰ-clause. I = citing a fact in corroboration; II = introducing one of two opposed clauses ('even if'); III = the protasis of a conditional sentence.
code_legend.capital_A_to_D: Kind of supposition. A = Simple, B = General, C = Contrary to Fact, D = Future.
code_legend.lowercase_a_b: Time reference. a = Present, b = Past.
code_legend.number: The specific verb construction (mood/tense combination) in that cell.
code_legend.note: (D) Future Suppositions is the largest section and is a long numbered enumeration, hence citations like '(D) (56)'.

citation_scheme.iliad_books: CAPITAL Greek letters Α-Ω = Iliad books 1-24.
citation_scheme.odyssey_books: lowercase Greek letters α-ω = Odyssey books 1-24.
citation_scheme.line: Followed by a line number, e.g. Α 39 = Iliad 1.39.
citation_scheme.double_protasis: A leading asterisk (*) marks a double protasis.
citation_scheme.bare_number: A bare number continues the previous book (Ν 111, 316 = 13.111 and 13.316).
citation_scheme.resolution_status: All citations are resolved to {corpus, book, line} in the dataset.

qa.method: Extracted Iliad citations were cross-validated against an independent Homeric dependency treebank: does the cited introducing word occur at the line the table cites?

review_queue_resolution.method: Every citation flagged by the treebank cross-check was independently re-verified against our own served Iliad text (data/corpus/homerus-epic.ilias.jsonl, Perseus grc2 edition) by reading the cited line and its neighbors. This is a second, fully independent source from the treebank used in the original QA.
review_queue_resolution.outcome_summary: All 10 reviewed citations confirmed against the served Iliad. 0 line-number corrections applied; 0 still flagged. The treebank could not confirm them because of elision (ὅτʼ / ὅθʼ for ὅτε), differing syntactic tagging (εἰ, ἐπεί, ὡς), or lemma-grouping of a Cf. pointer (ὅς 9.140) - none was an OCR line-number error. The known false alarm ὅτε 2.395 was not re-checked (treebank scope-gate artifact, per the handoff).

items.served_text: εἰ δʼ ἂν ἐγὼ τούτους μὲν ὑποκλονέεσθαι ἐάσω
items.table_protasis: εἰ δ' ἂν τούτους ὑποκλονέεσθαι ἐάσω
items.evidence: The word εἰ and essentially the whole protasis are present at the cited line in our served Iliad. Not an OCR error; the treebank simply did not tag this εἰ δ' ἄν as a conditional protasis.

items.served_text: ὅς τʼ ἐπεὶ ἄρ κε κάμῃσι κύνας τʼ ἄνδρας τʼ ἐρεθίζων,
items.evidence: ἐπεὶ ... κε κάμῃσι is present at the cited line; the apodosis ἰθύει follows at 17.661. Treebank tagging difference, not an OCR error.

items.served_text: αἴ κε μετʼ Ἀργείην Ἑλένην κάλλισται ἔωσιν.
items.evidence: 9.140 is a valid conditional-relative line in our served Iliad (αἴ κε ... ἔωσιν, subjunctive). It is a Cf. pointer grouped under the relative-pronoun lemma ὅς; the relative pronoun itself (ὅς) sits three lines later at 9.143. The parallel citation in the same cf-list, ὅς 9.282, lands on the exactly parallel αἵ-κε line (served 9.282 = 'αἵ κε μετʼ Ἀργείην...'), with its ὅς likewise at 9.285. Two parallel citations both landing on the αἴ/αἵ-κε line rules out a random digit misread. The line number is correct; only the ὅς word-label is a cf-grouping artifact. No line correction applied.

items.served_text: τὰς διαπέρσαι ὅτʼ ἄν τοι ἀπέχθωνται περὶ κῆρι·
items.evidence: ὅτε is present in elided form ὅτʼ at the cited line. The treebank cross-check missed it because it matched whole tokens and ὅτʼ is elided.

items.served_text: ἄχνυται ἐν θυμῷ, ὅθʼ ὑπὲρ σέθεν αἴσχεʼ ἀκούω
items.evidence: ὅτε is present as the elided, aspirated form ὅθʼ (ὅτε elided before the rough breathing of ὑπέρ) at the cited line. Missed by the whole-token treebank check.

items.served_text: οἴκαδʼ ἄγῃ ὅτʼ ἂν αὖτε νεώμεθα πατρίδα γαῖαν.
items.evidence: ὅτʼ ἂν ... νεώμεθα is present verbatim at the cited line (elided ὅτʼ).

items.served_text: κρηῆναι δὲ καὶ ἄλλῳ, ὅτʼ ἄν τινα θυμὸς ἀνώγῃ
items.evidence: Exact match: ὅτʼ ἄν τινα θυμὸς ἀνώγῃ is present at the cited line (elided ὅτʼ).

items.served_text: αὐτὰρ ὅτʼ ἐς νῆάς τε ἴδοι καὶ λαὸν Ἀχαιῶν,
items.evidence: ὅτʼ ἐς νῆας ... ἴδοι is present at the cited line (elided ὅτʼ).

items.served_text: εἴλυται καθύπερθʼ, ὅτʼ ἐπιβρίσῃ Διὸς ὄμβρος·
items.evidence: ὅτε is present in elided form ὅτʼ at the cited line.

items.served_text: ἀλλʼ ἄγεθʼ ὡς ἂν ἐγὼ εἴπω πειθώμεθα πάντες·
items.evidence: ὡς is present at the cited line (ὡς ἂν ἐγὼ εἴπω, a conditional-relative 'as I shall bid'). Treebank tagged it as a comparative adverb rather than a conditional word; not an OCR error.

known_minor_ocr_slips.note: Minor accent slips seen on sanity pages; the Greek is otherwise faithful. Left as-is (known-minor), not corrected.
examples: αἰ for αἴ (visible in the leaf_447 title line 'εἰ (αἰ)')

files.description: Primary structured dataset: 153 construction cells. Each cell has code, protasis_mood, apodosis_mood, heading, examples[], cf_refs[], page, leaf. Each example has kind (conditional/relative/conditional_relative), intro_word, protasis, apodosis, english, and refs[] with {corpus: il|od, book, line, ref, double_protasis}.
Per-introducing-word citation index: word -> construction code -> {il:[refs], od:[refs], examples[]}. Answers what a lexicon cross-reference such as 'see Table at end III.B.a' actually cites.
Intermediate per-page structured cells produced before the final merge into cunliffe_appendix.json. Retained for provenance/reproducibility; the two files above are the authoritative outputs.
QA summary: per-word counts, the independent cross-check of Iliad citations, and the original review queue.
